items.claim: The single-proverb boundary at Prov.20.17 holds; the row correctly reads the opening token as the stative adjective for pleasantness rather than importing the surety-verb sense from the adjacent verse.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.20.17 opens עָרֵ֣ב (byte tier), the qatel-pattern adjective 'sweet/pleasant', while oshb:Prov.20.16 carries the homographic root in עָ֣רַב (byte tier), Qal perfect 'he pledged/gave surety' -- same three root consonants, different stative pattern, so the root collision is not cohesion evidence. The row's device_notes 'synthetic couplet' tracks the Hebrew vav-clause as a plain temporal connector; WEB renders it “but afterwards” (web:Prov.20.17), yet the row's label does not lean on that English adversative, so there is no translation-dependent slippage.

items.claim: device_notes labels Prov.20.23 a synthetic couplet, but the row's own rationale describes the second colon as restating the same commerce concern from a different angle, which is a synonymous relationship, not a synthetic one, and the Hebrew colon structure supports the restatement reading over progression.
items.evidence: Colon A תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה אֶ֣בֶן וָאָ֑בֶן (byte tier, oshb:Prov.20.23) and colon B וּמֹאזְנֵ֖י מִרְמָ֣ה לֹא טֽוֹב (byte tier) both render the same evaluative judgment (abomination to Yahweh / not good) over two closely paired instruments of commercial fraud (differing weights / dishonest scales), joined by a plain vav with no adversative marker and no new action or consequence introduced. WEB likewise joins the halves with a bare “and” (web:Prov.20.23), giving no antithetic or additive-progression signal in either witness. span/unit_type are unaffected; this is a parallelism-class defect in device_notes measured against the row's own colon evidence and its own rationale wording.

items.claim: The row calls the qere תַּמְר֣וּק 'the verb for that cleansing', but the pointed byte is a noun functioning as predicate of a verbless clause, and WEB's verb rendering looks like the source of the mislabel rather than the Hebrew part of speech.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.20.30 reads חַבֻּר֣וֹת פֶּ֭צַע תמריק תַּמְר֣וּק בְּרָ֑ע וּ֝מַכּ֗וֹת חַדְרֵי בָֽטֶן (byte tier): a nominal clause, 'bruises of a wound [are] a cleansing/scouring against evil', with תַּמְר֣וּק standing as the predicate noun (segholate-pattern noun) over the ketiv תמריק -- the row does correctly disclose this as a ketiv/qere note (pmarks, single witness; Prov.20.30 confirmed against pmarks_Prov.json kq, count 1). But 'the verb for that cleansing' calls the qere a verb; the staged extract carries no morphology layer, so this is argued from the pointed bytes alone: the noun pattern and its nominal-predicate position in a verbless clause both point away from a finite-verb reading. WEB's own rendering supplies the English verb “cleanse away” (web:Prov.20.30), which is the likely source of the slip -- an English verb standing in for a Hebrew noun. This does not change the span or unit_type.

items.claim: The single-proverb boundary at Prov.21.1 holds; the opener claim and the refusal to treat the shared divine name with Prov.21.2 as a cohesion driver both check out against the bytes.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.21.1 opens the verse פַּלְגֵי מַ֣יִם לֶב מֶ֭לֶךְ בְּיַד יְהוָ֑ה עַֽל כָּל אֲשֶׁ֖ר יַחְפֹּ֣ץ יַטֶּֽנּוּ (byte tier) with a bare metaphor, no comparative preposition, matching the row's 'applied metaphorically' language rather than WEB's added simile “like the watercourses” (web:Prov.21.1). Both oshb:Prov.21.1 and oshb:Prov.21.2 carry the unprefixed divine name at byte tier; no other content token is shared between the two verses, so treating the recurring name as texture rather than a boundary driver is byte-consistent.

items.claim: The single-proverb boundary at Prov.21.2 holds; the antithetic label is grounded in the Hebrew's own subject/predicate contrast, not merely in WEB's inserted 'but'.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.21.2 reads כָּֽל דֶּרֶךְ אִ֭ישׁ יָשָׁ֣ר בְּעֵינָ֑יו וְתֹכֵ֖ן לִבּ֣וֹת יְהוָֽה (byte tier, full verse) -- 'every way of a man is right in his own eyes' set against 'and Yahweh weighs the hearts', a genuine subject/predicate contrast (human self-perception vs. divine measurement) independent of WEB's “but Yahweh weighs the hearts” (web:Prov.21.2). No content token beyond the divine name is shared with the adjacent verses, consistent with the row's rejected_alternative.

items.claim: The single-proverb boundary at Prov.21.9 holds; the row's tov-opener claim is confirmed against the book's tov-opener inventory and the comparative construction is accurately described.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.21.9 opens ט֗וֹב (byte tier); Prov.21.9 is listed among the 16 tov-opener verses in prov_device_inventory.json (tov_openers). The verse is a tov-min comparative clause, not a synonymous or antithetic pairing, so 'synthetic couplet' is a defensible catch-all label. No shared vocabulary links Prov.21.8 or Prov.21.10 to this verse.

items.claim: The single-proverb boundary at Prov.21.15 holds; the antithetic label matches the Hebrew's joy/ruin, righteous/evildoer contrast, and the row correctly reads the gapped predicate across both cola.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.21.15 reads שִׂמְחָ֣ה לַ֭צַּדִּיק עֲשׂ֣וֹת מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּ֝מְחִתָּ֗ה לְפֹ֣עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן (byte tier); the doing-of-justice predicate is the gapped subject for the second colon -- the same act is joy to the righteous, ruin to evildoers -- which the row's 'naming that same justice a ruin' language reflects. No shared token with Prov.21.14 or Prov.21.16.

items.claim: The single-proverb boundary at Prov.21.22 holds; the vav-consecutive sequence supports the synthetic-couplet label, and the row's no-catchword claim against Prov.21.21 and Prov.21.23 checks out.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.21.22 reads עִ֣יר גִּ֭בֹּרִים עָלָ֣ה חָכָ֑ם וַ֝יֹּ֗רֶד עֹ֣ז מִבְטֶחָֽה (byte tier) -- the closing clause opens with a vav-consecutive verb, a progressive action (scaling, then toppling) rather than synonymous restatement or antithesis, matching 'synthetic'. No content token is shared with Prov.21.21 or Prov.21.23.
